brief.deck: PayPal named Antonio Lucio Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer on 29 April 2026, inside a reorganisation into three businesses under new CEO Enrique Lores, effective 2 June. Both men ran HP when it became Ferrari's title partner in 2024. A $33.2B-revenue payments brand has a Formula 1-literate top team.
brief.the_case_p1: On 29 April PayPal announced a reorganisation into three operating units, Checkout Solutions & PayPal, Consumer Financial Services & Venmo, and Payment Services & Crypto, effective 2 June, with Antonio Lucio joining from HP as Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer and Diego Scotti departing. It is the first structural move by Enrique Lores, President and CEO since 1 March after six years running HP. The base is large: 2025 revenue of $33.2B, total payment volume of $1.79T and net income of $5.2B, reported on 3 February.
brief.the_case_p2: The pair have done this before. HP announced its multi-year title partnership with Ferrari on 24 April 2024 with Lores as CEO and Lucio as chief marketing and corporate affairs officer; the HP livery debuted at the Miami GP weeks later. PayPal already buys sports, a Phoenix Suns jersey patch since 2018 and the PayPal Park naming rights in San Jose, yet has nothing in Formula 1 while Visa, Mastercard and American Express do.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Lucio takes the chair on 2 June with a mandate to rebuild the brand under a new CEO; first-hundred-day platform decisions are made before the summer. The European rounds from Monaco, then the US GP and Las Vegas, sit inside the window, and teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief.why_team_para: Ferrari's roster has no payments partner: the finance names are UniCredit, BingX, Vantage and AON, and HP is the title partner that Lores and Lucio signed from the other side of the table. That relationship is the warm path: the two executives who put HP on the car know Maranello's commercial team, its hospitality and its e-commerce audience. Ferrari's global fan base and merchandise business give a checkout and wallet brand a real transaction surface.
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. PayPal and Venmo as the checkout and wallet layer for Ferrari's fan commerce: the online store, ticketing and hospitality bookings, Esports and Driver Academy programmes, with Pay Later at checkout for high-ticket merchandise and Venmo for the US fan base at the US GP and Las Vegas. In return: Official Payments Partner designation, paddock hospitality for merchant and enterprise clients, and content alongside the HP programme.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Payments Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, matching Lucio's brand-rebuild horizon. Estimated $8-12M a year, part in kind via checkout integration. Scope: rear-wing endplate or halo placement, checkout and wallet integration across store and ticketing, US-round hospitality, and a co-branded Pay Later and Venmo campaign around the US rounds.

Antonio Lucio joins from HP as Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer and Anshu Bhardwaj becomes Chief AI Transformation & Simplification Officer; Diego Scotti and Michelle Gill leave.

why_now.label: A new CEO's first move

Brand rebuilds follow structures like this, and the executive who will run it arrives on 2 June.

why_now.label: The base
why_now.text: PayPal reported 2025 net revenue of $33.2B, up 4%, total payment volume of $1.79T, up 7%, and net income of $5.2B on 3 February 2026. It already spends on sport at scale: a Phoenix Suns jersey patch since 2018, extended through the 2026 NBA season, and the PayPal Park naming rights in San Jose.

why_now.text: From the 7 May row date the European rounds run from Monaco through Monza; the US GP and Las Vegas fall in the last quarter of the calendar. Teams close their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a conversation opened in May lands as Lucio takes the seat and can be announced at a US round.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Ferrari's roster carries HP as title partner and UniCredit, BingX, Vantage and AON on the finance side; there is no payments, wallet or checkout partner. Official Payments Partner is a clean category at the team with the largest global following.

why_team.label: The warm path
why_team.text: HP announced its multi-year Ferrari title partnership on 24 April 2024 with Enrique Lores as CEO and Antonio Lucio as Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer; the livery debuted at the Miami GP that May. The two executives now running PayPal have negotiated with Maranello's commercial team, sat in its hospitality and seen its fan-commerce numbers. That is a leadership tie of the warmest class.

why_team.label: A team that will use the product
why_team.text: Ferrari sells to fans directly: store, tickets, hospitality, esports. PayPal's checkout, Pay Later and Venmo are used in the transaction, not just shown on the car, which separates a payments partner from a logo.

why_team.label: Why not the US-first alternative
why_team.text: Cadillac's debut roster has no finance partner and PayPal is a San Jose company, so the American entry was weighed. It was not chosen: it has no relationship path, no comparable fan-commerce volume in year one, and the Ferrari tie is the asset the desk can activate now. Cadillac stays the fallback if Ferrari's board declines a payments partner.

## The trigger

Company-announced: PayPal newsroom, 29 Apr 2026, "PayPal Announces Strategic Reorganization to Accelerate Growth" (also filed as an 8-K exhibit and carried by PRNewswire). Three operating units effective 2 June 2026; Antonio Lucio joins as Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer; Diego Scotti departs effective 2 June (Marketing Week, Adweek). Signal date 29 Apr 2026, eight days before the row date.

## The leadership tie (the warmest signal class)

HP announced its multi-year Ferrari title partnership on 24 Apr 2024 (hp.com press kit; ferrari.com). Enrique Lores was HP's CEO (Nov 2019 to Feb 2026, Wikipedia) and is quoted in the announcement; Antonio Lucio had rejoined HP as EVP & Global Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer from January 2024 (Adweek, Nov 2023). The brief says they were CEO and CMO when HP signed Ferrari; it does **not** claim Lucio personally negotiated the deal, because no source says so. `leadership_ties`: Lores and Lucio, HP–Ferrari title partnership, 2024.

## Screen-outs and things not claimed

- **No PayPal or Venmo motorsport deal found** (search of F1 sponsor listings for 2025-26; sponsor table has no row). If one exists it would change the case.
- **Ferrari's fan-base size and merchandise revenue** are not quantified: no figure was sourced, so the copy says "global fan base" without a number.
- **Deal size ($8-12M a year) is an ESTIMATE**, labelled as such.
- **Employee count** (Revelio, ~23,900) is secondary data and was left out.
- **Lucio's Visa CMO spell** was not verified this session and is not claimed; "earlier CMO of Facebook" comes from Campaign US and Adweek.
- **HP optics** is the second risk: the two executives just left Ferrari's title partner. The counter is to size and structure the deal independently of HP.
- **Score 83, not the row's 90:** urgency is 13 (no deadline; Visa, Mastercard and American Express entrenched, Amex at league level) and Lucio is not in the seat until 2 June.

## Decision path

Antonio Lucio, Chief Marketing & Corporate Affairs Officer from 2 June 2026 (the sponsorship owner). Path: Enrique Lores, President & CEO (1 Mar 2026); Jamie Miller, Chief Financial and Operating Officer (interim CEO Feb 2026); Frank Keller, President, Checkout Solutions & PayPal. Source: PayPal newsroom releases of 3 Feb and 29 Apr 2026.

## Team choice

Ferrari over Cadillac. Cadillac's debut roster has no finance partner and PayPal is a US company, but the Ferrari path is the relationship the desk can activate now, and Ferrari's fan commerce is the Mode A surface. Every payments-conflicted team is named in `ruled_out` from the sponsor table.
